name: RealPLKSR
plain: RealPLKSR (neosr, after PLKSR by Lee et al., 2024): a large-kernel CNN upscaler; `realplksr-nomoswebphoto-x4` is Philip Hofmann's x4 model for noisy, blurred and JPEG / WebP-compressed photos; also loads other RealPLKSR checkpoints. Apache-2.0 code, CC-BY-4.0 weights.
summary: RealPLKSR (neosr; after PLKSR, Lee et al., 2024): a real-world super-resolution CNN of partial large-kernel blocks (3 x 3 channel mixer, a 17 x 17 conv on a quarter of the channels, element-wise attention, GroupNorm) and a pixel-shuffle upsampler. `realplksr-nomoswebphoto-x4` is Philip Hofmann's 4xNomosWebPhoto_RealPLKSR, an x4 model for photos with noise, lens blur and JPEG / WebP compression. `load(path)` reads other RealPLKSR checkpoints with the pixel-shuffle upsampler (any scale, width and depth).

papers.title: Partial Large Kernel CNNs for Efficient Super-Resolution

task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: the restored (upscaled) image, `model.scale` x the input size, RGB in [0, 1]. `tile=` runs large images in overlapping tiles (as ComfyUI).

variants.name: realplksr-nomoswebphoto-x4

licence.training_note: Release notes: Nomos-v2 (6000 photos, neosr's dataset) with realistic noise, lens blur, JPEG and WebP degradations; pretrained from neosr's 4x_realplksr_gan_pretrain.

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 1, resized or padded inside the model

original16.protocol: median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls
original16.note: .half() on 1 modules, fp16 inputs; neosr realplksr eval mode, float32, net(lq) clamped

portable.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

kernels.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

quality.title: DIV2K validation (every 2nd: 50 images), bicubic x4 LR -> HR, PSNR / SSIM (Y)
quality.protocol: DIV2K validation HR images and the official bicubic LR images (x4 or x2, the model's scale), one pass without tiles; PSNR and SSIM (Gaussian 11 x 11, sigma 1.5) on the Y channel (BT.601) of the output rounded to uint8, `scale` px border cropped, averaged over the images. Real-ESRGAN is trained for real-world degradations, not bicubic, so its PSNR is low: the numbers compare our modes with the original, not with PSNR-oriented upscalers.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1.4e-06 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.00047 and p99 <= 0.0018 (absolute error of the output `image`).
